premise: strawberry catches her husband with the eggplant at the farmers market
story:
🍓 The Receipt in the Melon Crate

Star Strawberry had always been the one people watched, and that Saturday the farmers market watched her walk past the melon crates with her chin up and her hands 🤚 shaking. She had rehearsed the lie for eleven days. Peter Banana waited by the honey stall 🍯 holding two coffees like a man who still believed in his own marriage. He kissed her cheek. He asked about her morning. He did not mention the receipt 🧾 folded in his back pocket.

Enzo Eggplant arrived at ten, the way he always did, in sunglasses 🕶 he did not need and a linen shirt he could not afford. Star felt the old heat rise in her throat. Three weeks of stolen afternoons, and every one of them had felt like weather 🌦 — something that happened to her rather than something she chose. Across the aisle, Bianca Broccoli was buying plums 🟣 she had no intention of eating, and watching.

The confrontation came fast and quiet. Peter set the coffees down, unfolded the receipt, and read the address of the motel out loud in the voice he used for grocery lists 💔. Star did not deny it. What she said instead was worse. "How long have you known?" And Peter, who had never once surprised her in eleven years, said, "Since the first afternoon."

Because Peter had not discovered anything. Peter had been told. Bianca Broccoli had walked into his office in the spring with a folder 📁 and a proposal, and Peter Banana, who could never say no to anyone and least of all to his mother-in-law, had agreed to wait, and to watch, and to let his wife ruin herself in public where the family lawyer could see it.

That was the first thing Star had not known. The second arrived eleven seconds later, when Enzo Eggplant crossed the aisle, set an envelope 📩 on the melon crate, and said he was finished. Bianca had hired him in February. Six payments, one seduction, one witness statement, and the Broccoli estate would pass cleanly to the grandchildren with Star cut out of it entirely. Enzo had taken five payments. He had refused the sixth, because somewhere in the third week he had stopped performing 🖤, and that ruined everything for Bianca, who needed a liar, and for Star, who had been counting on one.

Bianca's plums hit the pavement. She reached for the envelope and Enzo slid it out of her reach ✋ with the same lazy grace he used for everything. Inside, he said, were forty minutes of recordings 🎧 — her instructions, her prices, her exact words about her own daughter.

And Star Strawberry laughed 😶‍🌫️, not the laugh of a woman caught but the laugh of a woman watching a long plan finally land.

Because she had known about February since February. Enzo had told her the night he refused the money, and together they had decided to let Bianca keep building 🧩 the trap, all the way to the melon crates, in front of the whole market, where it could never be taken back. The affair had been real. The recordings had always been hers.

What none of them had planned for was Peter, who picked up the envelope nobody was guarding, opened it, and went very still ❄ — because the recordings were not the only thing inside. There was a single sheet of paper, dated four years ago, with a clinic letterhead 📄 and two names on it, and neither of those names was Enzo's. "Star," he said, and his voice had nothing left in it at all. "Whose is this?"
